=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:37-42 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The prerequisite check applies only to bundle members added after the pick, so the anchor (chosen at line 37 as the highest-ranked conflict-free candidate) can have an unshipped prerequisite outside the bundle and still be recommended, alone or as the bundle anchor.
  WHY: The orchestrator's issue DAG can only order the plans it is given, so the recommendation is not startable as specified. Severity disagreement: anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 rated NIT (confidence 3), the other three rated MAJOR (confidence 4), and the highest is used.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:37-40 (step 6 "Pick." bullet at line 37 and the new "Prerequisites satisfied" bullet at line 40) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The new prerequisite rule applies only to candidates added after the pick. Step 5 (line 24) treats missing prerequisites only as a ranking penalty, so an anchor with an unshipped prerequisite outside the bundle can still anchor a bundle.
  WHY: `/audit-plans` can print a bundle whose anchor depends on a plan not in the bundle, which the orchestrator cannot order. Single-plan recommendations already behave this way, but the PR adds the rule for members and leaves the anchor out.
- HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS: tests/test_audit_plans_command.py, in test_bundle_requires_relatedness_and_caps and test_implement_plan_ai_dispatches_a_bundle_once. The tests do not pin the "Prerequisites satisfied" bullet, the independent-file exclusion, the duplicate-path rule, the project-summary path-naming instruction, or the phase-counting phrases. Suggested fix: add `assert` lines against `step6` and `ipa` (about 5 lines). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:37, 40 (also cites 24, 36, 38, 42) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The prerequisite gate at line 40 scopes itself to bundle members. The anchor is selected at line 37 with no prerequisite check, and step 5 ranking (line 24) only demotes plans with missing prerequisites. The single-plan hand-off at line 42 then dispatches the anchor as-is.
  WHY: The orchestrator's DAG cannot sequence an anchor against an unshipped prerequisite that is outside the project, so the dispatch starts work before the plan is startable. The rule is applied asymmetrically to members only.
- HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS: tests/test_audit_plans_command.py, in test_bundle_requires_relatedness_and_caps (lines 92-97) and test_implement_plan_ai_dispatches_a_bundle_once (lines 105-114). The tests do not pin the "**Prerequisites satisfied:**" bullet at audit-plans.md:40. They also do not pin the implement-plan-ai.md:8, :41 and :43 additions ("drop repeats of the same resolved file", "fewer than 2 distinct plans remain", the branch/PR lookup-failure clause, and the project-summary path-naming sentence). Suggested fix: add assert lines to the existing tests, plus optionally one new test (about 5 lines). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:37-42 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The prerequisite check applies only to plans added as bundle members. The anchor is selected at line 37 without it, and line 42 still recommends the anchor alone when no member qualifies.
  WHY: `/audit-plans` can recommend an anchor with an unshipped prerequisite that is not in the project. The orchestrator DAG cannot sequence it, so the recommendation is not startable as specified.
- HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS: tests/test_audit_plans_command.py, in the bundle prerequisite contract tests. The tests do not pin that prerequisites are checked for the anchor as well as for members. Suggested fix: add a focused assertion that the anchor is rejected or skipped when it has an unshipped prerequisite outside the bundle (about 2 lines). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:37-42 (same content at workflow-templates/.claude/commands/audit-plans.md lines 37-42) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The prerequisite check gates only bundle members added after the pick. The "Pick." bullet at line 37 selects the anchor by value rank and the conflict screen only, and line 42 keeps the anchor as the single-plan recommendation. An anchor whose prerequisite is unshipped and is neither the anchor nor a member therefore passes.
  WHY: An audit run hands off a plan the orchestrator cannot start, reproducing the out-of-bundle-dependency defect the prerequisite bullet was meant to close. Every bundle starts from the anchor, so the gap sits at the rule's most impactful point.
- HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS: tests/test_audit_plans_command.py, in test_implement_plan_ai_dispatches_a_bundle_once (lines 105-114) and test_bundle_requires_relatedness_and_caps (lines 92-97). The "Prerequisites satisfied" bullet, the anchor-side prerequisite gap, the independent-file exclusion clause, the duplicate-path fallback and the phase-counting phrases are not pinned. Suggested fix: add asserts for "**Prerequisites satisfied:**" and "A candidate ranked lower only because a prerequisite was missing may join" in step6, and for "drop repeats of the same resolved file" and "a listed phase counts as missing" in ipa (about 4 lines). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
